item.title: Titans at Jaguars predictions: Will this be a repeat of Week 10?
item.description: Through 27 games as Jacksonville Jaguars head coach, Liam Coen has only lost back-to-back games once. The Jaguars lost to the Seattle Seahawks 20-12 on Oct. 12, 2025. The following week, they lost to the Los Angeles Rams 35-7 in London. Since then, over 20 regular season games, the Jaguars have lost just a total of four games, including three this season. When the Jaguars lost to the Denver Broncos in Week 2, they won three straight games. They then lost to the Houston Texans, followed by three more wins. Now, they are coming off a 23-18 loss to the New York Giants . Should the Jaguars lose to the Tennessee Titans on Nov. 29, it would mark just the second time Coen would have lost back-to-back games. Will that happen? Or do the Jags right the ship? Let's see what our Times-Union experts think. Last week, they were 1-6 and are 52-18 for the season. DEMETRIUS HARVEY Jaguars beat writer Jaguars 38, Titans 17 The Jaguars get back to what they do best: score points at home. Back at EverBank Stadium, Jacksonville has a chance to leave their poor play behind as they move into the most important part of their season. Season record: 8-2 (Lost last week) MIKE DiROCCO ESPN Jaguars 31, Titans 10 Bounceback game for Trevor Lawrence and the offense. Season record: 6-4 (Lost last week) RYAN O'HALLORAN Times-Union Sports columnist Jaguars 34, Titans 14 The Titans enter having allowed 43, 40 and 51 points in losses to Cincinnati, the Jaguars and Dallas, respectively. The last time they allowed at least 40 points in three consecutive games was 2004 (51, 52 and 41 points in losses). What am I getting that? This is a get-right game for the Jaguars’ offense after they committed eight penalties and had more turnovers (two) than touchdowns (one) in last week’s 23-18 loss to the New York Giants . Get back to running the football with efficiency after consecutive so-so games. Get back to having quarterback Trevor Lawrence posting a passer rating of at least 100. And get back to scoring 30-plus points. In the Jaguars-Titans game two weeks ago, Lawrence was lights out against extra pass rushers (7-of-8 passing for 84 yards) per my game charting. If Tennessee wants to get aggressive, look for Lawrence to have similar success. Season record: 8-2 (Lost last week) GARRY SMITS Times-Union Sports reporter Jaguars 34, Titans 13 Are the Titans playing defense with nine guys? One hand tied behind their back? Their shoelaces tied together? How else to explain giving up 44.6 points in their last three games? These guys couldn't stop a toddler on a tricycle. How leaky is this defense? To quote the immortal Wilford Brimley, when he provided the otherwise awful movie "Abcense of Malice," with its only good five minutes, "The last time there was a leak this bad Noah built hisself a boat." Season record: 8-2 (Won last week) JUSTON LEWIS Times-Union Sports reporter Jaguars 34, Titans 24 For as bad as the Jaguars looked against the Giants, they still lost by one score. item.title: What's college football's most overrated rivalry; predicting Texas vs A&M | Golden, Bohls
item.description: Texas Longhorns defensive end Colin Simmons (1) tries to sack Texas A&M Aggies quarterback Marcel Reed (10) during the first half of an NCAA college football game in the Lone Star Showdown in Austin, Texas, Friday, Nov. 28, 2025. (Ricardo B. Brazziell/Austin American-Statesman) Rivalry weekend is here, and Texas football has a lot on the line against the Texas A&M Aggies . The Lone Star Showdown will kick off late Saturday amid a slew of big games: Ole Miss vs. Mississippi State, Alabama vs. Auburn and more. We're also down to the final two rankings from the College Football Playoff . Will the committee finally get it right? And what about LSU and the SEC : Can they patch things up? MORE : Full preview for Texas vs Texas A&M RELATED: Ced's 5 biggest A&M-Texas games Columnists Cedric Golden and Kirk Bohls tackle the 10 key questions of the final week of the regular season: 1. What should Texas expect from Texas A&M on Friday? GOLDEN: A good fight. For a little while, at least. The oddsmakers got it right when they installed the Horns as an 11½- point favorite because these are clearly two teams on the opposite end of expectations. The Horns are prepping for the playoffs while the Aggies are wondering what the heck went wrong over this last couple of months. Arch Manning isn't perfect but he will be plenty good enough with those talented wideouts to put up enough points to get out of the 979 with a win. The defense holds strong in a 31-17 victory. BOHLS: If Mike Elko is smart, he'll start the game with an onside kick. After the Aggies recover, his first three plays should be a flea flicker, the Statue of Liberty and a triple reverse. Who cares if it's a three-and-out, it'd be fun. Now the trick plays would only delay the inevitable because Texas defense vs. A&M offense is a horrible matchup for the maroon, the Aggies have 12 sacks all year and Arch Manning is built for this in a 27-10 Longhorn win. 2. Is Mike Elko the guy to fix the Aggies? GOLDEN: I believe so. I've been Team Elko since he got here but Year 3 has been troubling in several areas. The new-look offensive line has flopped and the decision to promote Holman Wiggins from wide receivers coach to first-time play-caller is an unmitigated disaster as evidenced by quarterback Marcel Reed's precipitous drop in production. Defensive is Elko's calling card and that hasn't been the problem - the Aggies are seventh in the SEC - but must get an offensive mind in there to get it back on track. Nearly as important, Elko must set aside petty distractions ( stay off the message boards ) and get back to being a hard-nosed, accountable coach. The seat isn't hot just yet but it can get that way in a hurry. Texas A&M head football coach Mike Elko prepares to lead his team onto the field against the Missouri Tigers on Oct 10, 2026 at Memorial Stadium in Columbia, Mo. item.title: Fantasy Football Week 12 tight end rankings
item.description: Fantasy football managers have several important lineup decisions to make at tight end heading into the weekend of Week 12. With the Wednesday and Thursday matchups already done, these rankings focus exclusively on players scheduled to take the field later in the week. Here are the Week 12 fantasy football tight end rankings. MORE: Latest report is bad news for Kyren Williams fantasy football owners Top 10 Sep 20, 2026; Atlanta, Georgia, USA; Carolina Panthers tight end Darren Waller (88) celebrates after scoring a touchdown during the third quarter against the Atlanta Falcons at Mercedes-Benz Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Dale Zanine-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) 10. Darren Waller-Panthers: Waller has built a nice chemistry with QB Bryce Young. Heading into Tampa Bay, he’ll need it. The Bucs will be playing like their lives are on the line…their playoff lives will be. Waller is a top 15 fantasy TE who is tied for seventh in TDs. 9. Juwan Johnson-Saints: Johnson is heading to Cincinnati this week to face a Bengals team that will surely put up a ton of pts. Johnson is one of the only weapons the Saints have and will need to deploy him often for the Saints to even keep up. Johnson has similar numbers to Waller and is tied with him with four TDs. 8. Hunter Henry-Patriots: The Patriots offense has been struggling all year, even when they were healthier…but now they are without their top two WRs…and their starting QB. The best friend to a backup QB is often the TE, who is always there for a checkdown. Look for Henry to have a big game at SoFi Stadium this week. 7. Tyler Warren-Colts: And speaking of a team without many weapons…we have the Colts. Warren is tied for seventh among TEs in receptions and will be heavily targeted in this game. Anthony Richardson has been thrust into the starting role with Daniel Jones waived. He’ll need to rely heavily on Warren in the game this week against the Giants. 6. Brock Bowers-Raiders: Bowers didn’t play last week but is expected to suit up this week in Cleveland. If he ultimately plays, Bowers is a no-brainer, but monitor his status. Hockenson (87) reacts after scoring a touchdown against the Indianapolis Colts in the second half at U.S. Bank Stadium. TJ Hockenson-Vikings: Hockenson has been a top 10 TE in the league for eight seasons and is a true professional week in and week out. He’s seventh among TEs in receptions and should have a nice game with home-field advantage against the Falcons, with another week of practice with Kirk Cousins at the helm. 4. item.title: Canucks Rundown: Lineup Notes Vs. Flyers, Vancouver Mayor on Practice Facility
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Black Friday’s Canucks Rundown will preview the game against the Philadelphia Flyers and provide a practice facility update. Lineup Notes: Lankinen Could Return The Vancouver Canucks will face off against the Philadelphia Flyers in a Friday matinee game. The exact team deployment will be confirmed during warmups this afternoon in Philadelphia. There is reason to believe that Kevin Lankinen will get the start, following a tough outing for Leevi Merilainen , stopping 21 of 26 shots against the Detroit Red Wings on Wednesday . If Lankinen does start, it will be his first start since Nov. 3. Projected Lineup: DeBrusk-Chytil-Boeser Öhgren-Rossi-Lekkerimäki O’Connor-Mueller-Karlsson Reinhardt-Quillan-Cotter Buium-Hronek Pettersson-Willander Oleksiak-Schenn Lankinen A reminder that puck drop for Friday’s game will be at 1:00 p.m. PCT. Practice Facility Update Vancouver Mayor Pete Fry spoke to reporters on Thursday about Vancouver hosting the 2029 Grey Cup. During that press conference, Fry revealed that he would meet with the Canucks next week. One of the topics that will be discussed will be the much-awaited practice facility. Furthermore, The Province’s Patrick Johnston reported that Fry was interested in possibilities for a practice facility on Vancouver’s PNE grounds. Fry had been talking with minor hockey associations that have been lobbying for more ice rinks. Additionally, Vancouver Minor Hockey president Levi Higgs has suggested a practice rink be built north of the Pacific Coliseum, where a parking lot currently resides. It is located within the Hastings Park and PNE grounds. As a result, it sounds increasingly likely that the Canucks’ plans to use Britannia Rink as a practice facility will fall through. The Canucks are currently the only NHL team without plans for a practice facility. If there is a positive to take out of the season, getting the paperwork signed and sealed for a practice facility would be a great step in the right direction for the organization. Related Headlines Canucks Rundown: Malhotra Speaks on Effort, Cootes Update, Time for Lankinen The Anaheim Ducks Are Getting One Of The NHL’s Most Exciting Young Forwards Back LaMelo Ball’s Status Is Revealed After Scary Ankle Injury Read more at Sportsnaut

item.title: Kovač puts Gadou hype into perspective after Arsenal heroics
item.description: Kovač puts Gadou hype into perspective after Arsenal heroics Following his summer move from RB Salzburg, Joane Gadou has quickly established himself as a regular starter at the heart of Borussia Dortmund's defence. Most recently, the 19-year-old delivered a standout performance in Wednesday's 1-1 draw with Arsenal, earning widespread praise and sparking reports that a number of top European clubs are keeping tabs on him. Dortmund head coach Niko Kovač, too, is pleased with Gadou's development, but is keen to stress that the youngster still has plenty to learn. "I've said it time and time again: learning week after week in the Bundesliga is one thing, but the learning experience of playing against the best in the world in this sport every three days is many times greater," Kovač said at a press conference on Friday. "He is developing well and, like everyone else, still has areas where he can improve. But it would be far too easy if we were to say that he was already the finished article. He's not. But where he is at the moment, he is helping us a great deal. "He will be given all the time in the world and all the support he needs. He works hard at learning, and I like that. When you're learning, you're allowed to make mistakes too." Gadou has made 17 appearances for Dortmund so far this season.

item.title: Artemis III astronauts meet their spacecraft | Space photo of the day for Nov. 27, 2026
item.description: null NASA's Artemis III astronauts pose holding up three fingers to symbolize their mission as they visit the Orion spacecraft they will ride to space. (Image credit: NASA/Kim Shiflett) Training for a mission to space is hard work. But sometimes you have to take a minute and have a little fun with your crewmates. What is it? Crowded together with the Orion spacecraft, the four astronauts that make up the Artemis III crew hold up three fingers, taking a brief pause in their rigorous training for some lighthearted crew bonding. In the snapshot , the crew — from left to right, NASA astronauts Randy Bresnick (mission commander) and Frank Rubio (mission specialist), European Space Agency astronaut Luca Parmitano (mission pilot) and NASA astronaut Andre Douglas (mission specialist) — is spotted posing alongside the same Orion spacecraft that they will fly to space as part of their mission. This brief moment of levity took place where the spacecraft currently resides at the Neil A. Armstrong Operations and Checkout Building at NASA's Kennedy Space Center in Florida. Why is it incredible? This crew has a serious mission ahead of them. The four astronauts will launch to low-Earth orbit around Earth where they plan to practice rendezvous and docking with both Blue Origin and SpaceX's lunar landing vehicles , Blue Moon and Starship, respectively. To prepare, the crew has to undergo months of critical training to both be physically ready while prepared to handle any situation that might come up during their mission. And while Artemis III isn't landing astronauts on the moon, it is a critical step toward that goal. If Artemis III goes to plan and NASA has a lunar landing vehicle that passes rendezvous and docking tests with the Orion spacecraft, Artemis IV might see astronauts land on the moon for the first time since the final Apollo mission in 1972.

item.title: Lakers vs. Spurs: A Win Or Fake Title Claim
item.description: Feb 10, 2026; Los Angeles, California, USA; Los Angeles Lakers guard Bronny James (9) moves the ball against San Antonio Spurs forward Carter Bryant (11) during the second half at Crypto.com Arena. Mandatory Credit: Gary A. Vasquez-Imagn Images The Los Angeles Lakers face a make-or-break moment on Friday night in San Antonio. The stakes are higher than a single win in the standings. This matchup is the first true test for a roster that has been riding high. Redick Draws a Hard Line Lakers head coach JJ Redick did not mince words when asked about the pressure . Redick said, “We’re either going to be contenders or we’re going to be a fake team… If we win that [San Antonio] game and then we lose to Memphis and Houston, we’re back to being a fake team. So … the overreactions game-to-game are what they are, and we’ve got to, as a group, manage that and manage the noise and that’s just part of being in the NBA.” The Lakers have a 15-3 record, the best in the NBA. The Spurs are 15-4, a half-game behind. A loss to the Spurs would shatter the narrative of a championship-caliber team. The Spurs are not an easy opponent to beat. They had won 15 of their last 16 games before a recent loss. Victor Wembanyama is leading the charge with massive numbers. According to Yahoo Sports NBA , Wembanyama is averaging 30.7 points and 12.5 rebounds per game. He also blocks 3.8 shots a night while shooting 54.3% from the field. The Spurs have the best net rating in the league. They force teams to play in the paint, where they rank second in points. The Lakers must find a way to stop this dominant force or face a long night. Reaves Return Adds Hope Austin Reaves is one step closer to returning from a left heel bruise. He participated in a full practice on Wednesday after missing five games. His status for Friday remains undetermined, but his presence would change the offense. The Lakers have struggled without him, dropping to 18th in offensive rating. Before the injury, Reaves averaged 24.7 points and shot 40.9% from three. Redick noted the improvement in Reaves’ play during practice. Reaves echoed the sentiment, stating, “It felt good to play basketball again.” The team will see how he wakes up on Thursday before making a final call. Nine new players are on the roster and have never faced this level of scrutiny. Even Luka Doncic, who has played in big moments, has never been the face of a brand this large. The team must ignore the noise if they lose and move forward if they win. The game is the last NBA Cup qualifier for both sides. San Antonio is in a four-way tie for 2nd place with a 2-1 record, while the Lakers are 2-1. A win for Los Angeles secures their spot in the quarterfinals regardless of other results. The game tips off at 6:30 p.m. PT at the Frost Bank Center. It will air on Amazon Prime Video for fans to watch. This is the moment the season has been building toward for over a week. The Spurs are the measuring stick in the West now that the Thunder have been hit

item.title: Jaissle on Newcastle star’s fitness ahead of Brighton
item.description: Jaissle on Newcastle star’s fitness ahead of Brighton Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle says Tino Livramento is closing in on a return to the starting XI but insists the club will not rush him back. The defender featured against Arsenal last weekend following his spell out with injury, although Jaissle says a decision on whether he is ready to start has not yet been made, ahead of the game against Brighton. “Always better when we need to make decisions when it comes to the starting XI,” Jaissle said. “Tino, for example, is on his way back but we need to see if he is ready to start. “We still have two days. I don’t want to rush something. “He is such a fantastic footballer, we need to be smart with him.” Lewis Hall has also trained this week having been forced off with cramp against Arsenal. But Joelinton remains unavailable, with Jaissle reluctant to put a timeframe on his return, though says he is optimic of a return “sooner rather than later”.

item.title: Chelsea ramp up interest in Como starlet Jacobo Ramon as Blues make definitive Benoit Badiashile transfer call
item.description: FBL-EUR-C1-COMO-MAN UNITED - AFP Chelsea are looking to Serie A to bolster their defence in 2027, with Como centre-back Jacobo Ramon emerging as a key target at Stamford Bridge. While the Blues have made a firm decision on Benoit Badiashile's loan spell at Napoli, securing Ramon's signature will require fending off fierce competition from domestic and European rivals. Chelsea plot Serie A defensive overhaul Chelsea are preparing to strengthen their backline in 2027, with their recruitment strategy strongly tied to Serie A. According to The Athletic , the Blues are closely tracking Como centre-back Ramon as they look to add defensive reinforcements. Despite their plans to bolster the squad at the back, Chelsea have no intention of cutting short Badiashile's loan spell at Napoli. The club have decided against recalling any of their first-team loanees during the January transfer window. Rising star Ramon attracts major interest Ramon has caught the eye of decision-makers at Stamford Bridge, where the Spaniard is strongly admired. His impressive progress in Italy was recently rewarded with his first senior call-up to the Spanish national team . Chelsea are not the only English club keeping a close watch on the defender's development. Premier League rivals Arsenal and Manchester United have also been linked with Ramon in recent weeks, pointing towards a potentially competitive race for his signature. Real Madrid hurdle and Badiashile's Napoli stint Any club hoping to prise Ramon away from Como will have to navigate a notable complication. Although he is formally a Como player, Madrid hold an option to re-sign him at the end of the season, mirroring the arrangement they have in place for his team-mate Nico Paz. Meanwhile, Badiashile remains in Italy after moving to Napoli on loan last summer with a €27 million option to buy. The 25-year-old French defender has made five appearances across all competitions this season. Badiashile's campaign was recently interrupted by an injury that sidelined him for several weeks. However, he has now returned to group training with the Serie A side. Summer window key for Chelsea's defensive plans Chelsea supporters will have to remain patient regarding any potential move for Ramon. While the club admire the Como centre-back, a deal would only be possible in the summer transfer window rather than mid-season. With no January recalls planned for Badiashile or any other first-team loanees, the Blues will keep their current loan arrangements intact for the rest of the campaign. Attention will then turn to the summer market, where the Blues' pursuit of Ramon - and the interest from Arsenal, Manchester United, and Madrid - will come into sharper focus.

item.title: Giants sign .776 OPS outfielder after he spent 1 season with Yankees
item.description: Giants sign .776 OPS outfielder after he spent 1 season with Yankees originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The San Francisco Giants added outfield depth on Thanksgiving Day. According to Francys Romero , the AL West club signed center fielder Kenedy Corona to a minor league contract. "Venezuelan outfielder Kenedy Corona has agreed to a minor league contract with the San Francisco Giants, including an invitation to MLB Spring Training camp, according to sources," Romero wrote on X. Corona, 26, spent last season in Double-A and Triple-A in the New York Yankees system. In 102 games between the two levels, he hit .255/.349/.427 with 12 home runs, 53 RBIs, and a .776 OPS. MORE : Padres interested in re-signing 2.86 ERA starter despite $32M contract decision Corona made his Major League debut in 2025, suiting up for three games with the Houston Astros . He stepped up to the plate four times but did not record his first career hit. He's likely to start the season at Triple-A Sacramento with the Giants, but could provide solid outfield depth throughout the season. The New York Mets signed Corona as an international free agent from Venezuela in 2019. item.title: Ex-Iceland goalkeeper Ingvar Jonsson who was part of Euro 2016 squad that stunned England dies aged 37
item.description: Ingvar Jonsson, the former Iceland goalkeeper who was part of the squad that defeated England at the 2016 European Championship, has died at the age of 37. His former club Víkingur announced his death on Thursday. The team did not provide a cause of death, although Jonsson had reportedly been diagnosed with cancer earlier this year. In a statement, the Icelandic club said: "It is with great sorrow and deep sadness that we announce that our dear friend and teammate Ingvar Jonsson, goalkeeper for Víkingur, passed away on Wednesday, November 25, in the arms of his loved ones." They added: "The club and all of Víkingur are thinking of his family and loved ones. We send them our deepest condolences." Jonsson served as an unused substitute during Euro 2016 , when Iceland created one of the greatest shocks in tournament history by knocking England out in the round of 16. The team were later eliminated by France in the quarter-finals. Iceland stunned England at Euro 2016 (Jonathan Brady/PA) (PA Wire) Paying tribute on X, European football’s governing body Uefa wrote: "We extend our deepest condolences to Ingvar’s family, friends and former team-mates. Our thoughts are with them at this difficult time." Jonsson earned eight international caps for Iceland, having made his first squad back in 2012. He had to wait another two years before making his first appearance for his country in a friendly against Belgium. His final cap for Iceland came in 2019, but he continued to make the squad through until 2022. His club career saw him start at Njardvik in his homeland before moving to Norwegian outfit IK Start in 2015. He would go on to play for Sandnes Ulf and Sandefjord prior to leaving Norway in 2018 to join Danish side Viborg. After two years in Denmark, Jonsson returned to Iceland to play for Vikingur and remained at the club until his passing.

item.title: Padres May Have Edge In Seiya Suzuki Chase
item.description: Free agent outfielder Seiya Suzuki The San Diego Padres could use help in the outfield, and Seiya Suzuki makes sense as a target. Suzuki and Randy Arozarena are the two best hitters in free agency, and either one would be a great fit for the Padres. However, Arozarena reportedly prefers to sign on the East Coast. The Padres have reportedly shown interest in signing Suzuki, and according to Sanspo Japan , San Diego may have an edge over other suitors. "San Diego is one of the most comfortable environments for Seiya and his wife, Airi," a source told Sanspo Japan. Before Suzuki signed with the Chicago Cubs, the Padres were reportedly a potential landing spot for him. In fact, the Padres may have been his preferred choice. "If the salary and contract terms were the same for multiple interested teams, he would choose the Padres," a source told Sanspo Japan at the time. Suzuki has posted an OPS over .800 in each of the last four years, and was a great defender last year. He was a Gold Glove finalist, after defense had been a flaw in his game for years. The Padres could sign him to play right field and move Fernando Tatis Jr. to left field. They could also try to move Suzuki to left field, but it may not be wise to mess with his defense after he finally figured it out. More MLB: Tarik Skubal's Dad Reveals Why Son Chose Mets Over Proven Winners

item.title: Napoli star De Bruyne to miss Sassuolo clash
item.description: Napoli star De Bruyne to miss Sassuolo clash Napoli star Kevin De Bruyne will miss Sunday’s Serie A match against Sassuolo due to a muscle problem. The Belgium international trained separately at the Napoli training centre today and is not expected to be available for the upcoming Serie A match against Sassuolo at the Mapei Stadium. Injured De Bruyne to miss Sassuolo vs. Napoli TURIN, ITALY – NOVEMBER 01: Kevin De Bruyne of SSC Napoli passes the ball under pressure from Douglas Luiz of Juventus during the Serie A match between Juventus and SSC Napoli at Allianz Stadium on November 01, 2026 in Turin, Italy. (Photo by Valerio Pennicino/Getty Images) Sky says De Bruyne is not expected to be out of action for long, as he’s dealing with muscle fatigue that requires rest. Napoli already have a long list of injured players, with Alex Meret, Giovanni Di Lorenzo, Benoit Badiashile, Alisson Santos, Stanislav Lobotka, Alessandro Buongiorno and Antonio Vergara unavailable for the upcoming league game. NAPLES, ITALY – OCTOBER 10: Kevin De Bruyne of SSC Napoli scores a penalty for his team’s first goal during the Serie A match between SSC Napoli and Frosinone Calcio at Stadio Diego Armando Maradona on October 10, 2026 in Naples, Italy. (Photo by Francesco Pecoraro/Getty Images) Napoli have had a tough start to the season, sitting 8th in the Serie A table, nine points behind Milan in fourth. They’ve won only one of their last five games across all competitions, with two draws and two losses. De Bruyne, 35, is in his second season at Napoli and has four goals and two assists in 17 appearances across all competitions in 2026-27.

item.title: Deportivo coach wary of Barcelona quality ahead of La Liga clash: ‘We are going to have to suffer a lot’
item.description: Deportivo coach wary of Barcelona quality ahead of La Liga clash: ‘We are going to have to suffer a lot’ Following a 4-1 win over Sabah in the UEFA Champions League, Barcelona will resume their La Liga campaign this weekend as they take on Deportivo de A Coruna. It promises to be a tricky affair for the Catalans, having made a long journey to Baku in midweek, forcing Hansi Flick to make multiple changes to the squad. Speaking ahead of the clash, Deportivo coach Antonio Hidalgo talked about the prospect of facing Barcelona and how the team has evolved under Flick. Hidalgo wary of Barcelona Hidalgo started by giving utmost respect to Barcelona, calling them among the finest while praising the standards instilled by Flick. “Surely comes one of the best teams in the world,” he said. “I think Hansi has taken them to a very high level of competitiveness. They’re showing it every week.” “They have won all their matches except one against Madrid and the Champions League against PSG and with an average of four goals per game,” he added. Hidalgo has immense respect for Barcelona. (Photo by Juan Manuel Serrano Arce/Getty Images) The Deportivo coach had no doubts about the challenge waiting for his players, as he demanded total commitment from his team. “We know that we are going to have to suffer a lot without the ball, be very tight. We have to be willing to suffer, to compete at the highest level in all duels and be very intense ,” he added. Hidalgo on Barcelona’s key threat Hidalgo went on to talk about the intensity Barcelona show when out of possession. He singled out that counter-press as a key threat for Deportivo de A Coruna. “We know of the aggressiveness that Barça has without the ball, it puts you a lot of difficulty, especially in that robbery after loss they do,” he said. Despite the challenge, Hidalgo backed his home fans to provide the atmosphere and inspire his players. “With our fans we will be much more powerful, we know it . You always come out with the conviction of competing for matches. “ We are First Division teams and everything is equal. It will be a game of a lot of tension and we will have to compete it at the highest level ,” he said. Aubameyang is expected to feature against former club Barcelona this weekend. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images) Hidalgo on Barcelona past and Aubameyang relief The match carries personal significance for Hidalgo, who spent his early years in Barcelona’s academy. “I’m from Barcelona, from Canovelles, which is half an hour away. I have my whole family there. From 12 to 21 years old, I was in the Barça quarry,” he said. “When you face teams from that entity, you always see them in a different and special way ,” he added. Finally, Hidalgo confirmed that Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang, the former Barcelona forward, is fine after being left unharmed in a car crash ahead of the game. Source: Mundo Deportivo

item.title: Pochettino insists Manchester United must involve him in January transfer plans
item.description: Pochettino insists Manchester United must involve him in January transfer plans Mauricio Pochettino has said it is common sense for him to be involved in Manchester United 's recruitment plans. Manchester United are expected to invest in the January transfer window, as the club look to turn around their campaign. United are currently 19th in the Premier League table after 11 games. A centre-forward and additional defensive depth are understood to be on the agenda for the winter window, which will re-open on January 1, 2027. Pochettino was appointed as head coach on a two-and-a-half year deal this month, and was asked about potential signings on Friday. Speaking at his pre-match press conference ahead of facing Brentford, Pochettino said it would make little sense for him not to be prominent in recruitment plans. "In the future of course, but right now we are focused on trying to relate all of the ideas to the squad," Pochettino said when asked how he will work with the club's leadership. "It's not common sense if the head coach is not involved in situations that affect the build up of the squad. For me, that is a benefit for Manchester United. If I am not involved, and I coach players that you don't know or maybe you don't want, or you don't agree, that is not for me. "I respect all ways to work but I am going to take my responsibility and everyone is going to know that I am going to be involved. That is what we were talking [about] in the last few days. "Being the coach is not only to pick 11 players. It's to assess and analyse the work behind about how you build. The responsibility is massive from the coaching staff." Manchester United have addressed one squad issue by activating a one-year extension in Bruno Fernandes' contract. Fernandes' deal was due to expire in the summer but has been extended until 2028.

item.title: Villanova’s Last Win Looking Worse, Wildcats With Another Chance Friday
item.description: Villanova rebounded from a bad loss against Pitt with a victory over, at the time No. 18, Michigan. At the time, the Wolverines were ranked and this looked like a good win. While it still will hold some weight on the resume, the early-season win has taken a hit. Michigan was blown out by Creighton just three days later and on Thanksgiving Day, trailed by nearly 30 against Miami. Safe to say, this is not the Michigan team that won a National Championship last season as the roster has turned over. Now, this just means that Villanova won a game it should have. The loss would have been even worse if the Wildcats were to get tripped up. Villanova will have another chance for a statement performance on the road against Kansas. This is the most difficult game that the team will play in the non-conference. Kansas has a dominant win over Kentucky this season with its only loss coming against No. 1 Houston. The game being played at Allen Fieldhouse provides another challenge for Villanova. As a 12-point underdog, an upset victory in a true road game against Kansas would catapult this team. At the same time, a loss will not hurt the resume. This is a measuring stick game to see where the Wildcats currently sit this season.

item.title: Caitlin Clark couldn’t believe the Cowboys’ Thanksgiving Day collapse, either
item.description: Caitlin Clark couldn’t believe the Cowboys’ Thanksgiving Day collapse, either originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Like most football fans in the United States, Caitlin Clark was aghast as the Dallas Cowboys suffered the largest Thanksgiving Day game collapse in NFL history. Leading 31-10 over the Philadelphia Eagles late in the third quarter, the Cowboys contrived to lose, 39-38, when Philadelphia's Jake Elliott drilled a 60-yard field goal with two seconds remaining in regulation. MORE : Fever’s Caitlin Clark strengthens bond with Grammy-winning artist during WNBA offseason One of the key decisions that went against the Cowboys was Dallas opting to go for it on 4th-and-1 from the Philadelphia 40-yard line with 55 seconds remaining. The play was a disaster. Quarterback Dan Prescott was sacked for a loss of nine yards, giving the Eagles excellent field position to attempt the game-winning kick. Clark asked her followers on X to explain "what exactly" the Cowboys were trying to do. What exactly were the cowboys doing there — Caitlin Clark (@CaitlinClark22) November 27, 2026 Had Dallas picked up the yard and gotten a fresh set of downs, the Cowboys would have been able to run out the clock and hold on for the win as the Eagles were out of timeouts. Instead, the Cowboys opted to pass and risk a Prescott sack -- and the Eagles took full advantage. Clark is an avid NFL fan, and her own team, the Kansas City Chiefs, lost on a late field goal on Thanksgiving as well. But at least they didn't blow a 21-point lead at home. It could always be worse, as the Cowboys have proven repeatedly in the past three decades. item.title: Players Era Tournament: Tennessee-Louisville set for Michelob Ultra Arena bracket final
item.description: Nov 26, 2026; Las Vegas, NV, USA; Louisville Cardinals guard Seth Trimble (5) drives past. St. John's Red Storm guard Ian Jackson (11) during the first half of a semifinal game of the Players Era Sixteen tournament at Michelob Ultra Arena. Mandatory Credit: Candice Ward-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Tennessee Volunteers handled Iowa State on Thanksgiving afternoon, going into the night waiting to find out their next opponent. That opponent would come out of the Rick Pitino bowl, if you will. Pitino’s St. Johns team faced his old school Louisville late in Las Vegas, and the game delivered. The Johnnies came storming back after Louisville had total control, tying the game at 90 with just seconds left. Adrian Wooley drilled a corner three as time expired to send Louisville into a matchup against Tennessee. THE SHOT OF A LIFETIME. #GoCards pic.twitter.com/cAoNnurzr6 — Louisville Men's Basketball (@LouisvilleMBB) November 27, 2026 Tennessee and Louisville have played each of the last two seasons, with the Volunteers winning both in blowout fashion. It was a home and home for the series, with Tennessee winning by 20+ on each occasion. As per usual in today’s college basketball world though, none of that matters with completely new rosters on both sides. “Two years ago, they beat us by 790,” Louisville head coach Pat Kelsey joked. “Last year they beat us by 400. You know, we’ve gotten two good ol’ fashioned freakin’ butt whippings by those guys. “It’s gonna be another street fight. You know, you play Coach Barnes’ team — it is, it’s going to be bare knuckles, backyard brawl and we have to be ready to answer that physical challenge. The good news for us is that we have a tough, physical group of dudes.” Louisville, just like Tennessee, is armed with one of the top transfer portal classes in the country. Seth Trimble (UNC), Karter Knox (Arkansas) and Flory Bidunga (Kansas) lead the way for the Cardinals in scoring so far. Kelsey’s group is 5-1 overall, coming off of big wins over Texas Tech and of course St. Johns. Their lone loss came against Memphis, a game where the Cardinals blew a big lead in a disastrous second half. You’ve seen this talented roster at full song this week, however, which will give Tennessee a big challenge on Friday night. Will you see a letdown from Louisville after that emotional, last second win over Pitino? That has to be a real concern coming in. In the T-Mobile Arena final, Creighton will take on Gonzaga for the right to play the Tennessee-Louisville winner on Saturday night. How to watch Tennessee vs. Louisville in the Players Era Tournament Location : Las Vegas, Nevada (Michelob Ultra Arena) Time : 9 p.m. ET TV Channel : ESPN Streaming : ESPN App Odds : Louisville -1.5

item.title: ‘Would you approach LeBron James the same way?’ – A’ja Wilson’s agent calls out brands
item.description: Photo by Melissa Tamez/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images A’ja Wilson’s agent, Jade-Li English of Klutch Sports Group, has opened up about pushing brands to recognise who Wilson is. A’ja Wilson just locked up a record fifth WNBA MVP, her third in a row, after putting up 26.2 points, 9.4 rebounds, 3.2 assists, and 1.9 blocks on 52.7% shooting, before the Aces ran into Golden State in the semifinals. While she’s making $1.4 million on the court with Las Vegas, Forbes estimates she’s pulling in over $5 million off it from deals with Nike, Chase, AT&T, and more, showing how big the gap can still be between WNBA salaries and star endorsement money. A’ja Wilson’s agent demands more from brands Even as A’ja Wilson ’s commercial pull keeps growing, her agent says getting brands to truly meet her at her level hasn’t always been simple, pushing companies to see who she is as a Black woman and measure every pitch against how they’d treat an icon like LeBron James . In a recent interview with Forbes , A’ja Wilson’s agent, Jade-Li English of Klutch Sports Group, said she has had to have “difficult conversations” with brands to make sure they “understand who she is as a Black woman.” English says she asks them, “‘Would you go to a LeBron James and approach a partnership with him the same way that you would approach A’ja Wilson?’” LeBron James is pulling in $85 million off the court this season, sitting fourth overall in NBA earnings at $88.9 million, with just $3.9 million coming from his salary. Because the NBA has been bigger and around way longer than the WNBA, its stars have had more time to build massive global reach and brand value, which helps explain why James’s off-court haul beats what even top WNBA names make. Read more: Cathy Engelbert’s departure can ruin Fever’s GM plans with Allison Feaster, says analyst ‘Worse than Jalen Brunson on CSI’ – Fans react as Angel Reese makes Netflix appearance Caitlin Clark publicly questions Dallas Cowboys after embarrassing Thanksgiving loss

item.title: ‘New York is turning into Gotham City’: NBA star rips Zohran Mamdani’s plan to close Rikers Island
item.description: Jul 25, 2026; New York, NY, USA; New York City mayor Zohran Mamdani attends the USATF Championships at Icahn Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani recently unveiled his administration’s plan to close Rikers Island, which would replace the notorious jail complex with four borough-based jails across the city by the end of 2032. Not everyone is on board with the idea, including one NBA player. Milwaukee Bucks forward Kyle Kuzma blasted the plan in a viral video, arguing that it would put criminals back into their communities. Kuzma also joked that New York is “turning into Gotham City” and compared the plan to something the Joker would come up with. However, his criticism was riddled with factual inaccuracies. Mamdani’s Rikers Plan Mamdani’s administration released its plan to close Rikers on Nov. 20. Under the plan, the city will open a borough-based jail in Brooklyn in 2029, followed by the Bronx and Queens in 2031 and Manhattan in 2032. In announcing the plan, Mamdani said that the new jails would operate very differently than Rikers, which sits on an island in the East River. “These jails will look, feel and, most importantly, operate very differently than Rikers. Any family member of someone held at Rikers will tell you how isolating that jail is; how it can take hours to visit a loved one; how far away you feel from the rest of the city; how challenging it is for someone held there to see legal counsel and feel connected to any kind of support,” Mamdani said, according to a city transcript . “Not only will these borough-based jails be closer to courts and public transit, they will serve as hubs for the community of our entire city, with at least 20,000 square feet of separate community space at each one, open to everyday New Yorkers. This is not only how we integrate incarcerated New Yorkers back into our city, it is also how we lower recidivism rates,” he continued. ‘Gotham City’ In a video posted to social media this week, Kuzma criticized the plan to close Rikers. He kicked off his video with a warning for New Yorkers. “Knock knock, New York, we have a serious issue. We need the Bat-Signal. I don’t know where it is, but New York is turning into Gotham City,” Kuzma said, in a clip that has been viewed more than 2 million times on X . Kuzma then took aim at the plan to build jails in each borough. “You know, you have this Democratic Socialist Party, you know, because Mamdani is one right now. They are planning to close Rikers Island, a jail. And guess what they’re doing? They want to open up new jails in all the boroughs. So now they want to make these jails in the city community centers or a way to integrate criminals back into society. I thought the whole point of criminals getting away is to isolate them so they can learn their lesson. This doesn’t make no sense,” Kuzma said. “Most jails and prisons are terrible. item.title: NFC playoff picture: NFC East looks like two-horse race with Giants and Commanders
item.description: The Eagles celebrated an upset of the Cowboys on Thursday. | Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys’ stunning meltdown on Thursday night against the Philadelphia Eagles, blowing at 31-10 late-third quarter lead in a 39-38 defeat, changed the NFC East title race. The Washington Commanders are now the only team that appears to have a realistic chance of catching the first place New York Giants. As of Friday morning, NFL.com gives the Giants a 70% chance of making the playoffs. That rises to 78% if rthey defeat the Indianapolis Colts on Sunday. It falls to 53% should they lose. The Commanders currently sit with a 24% chance to make the playoffs. The Cowboys? NFL.com says Dallas (5-7) now has just an 8% chance of making the playoffs. With a two-game lead over the 4-5-1 Commanders, the Giants need to take care of their own business. This week’s game against the 3-8 Colts, likely the weakest team remaining on the Giants’ schedule, is critical. “I’m not really worried about what the Commanders and Cowboys (are doing). ,” Giants right tackle Jermaine Eluemunor said earlier this week. “I’m just going to keep my focus on winning every single week with the Giants. If we do what we need to do, then we’ll be exactly where we want to be come January.”

item.title: Antonelli leads Russell in Qatar first practice
item.description: Kimi Antonelli secured his maiden F1 title in Mexico City earlier this month [Getty Images] World champion Kimi Antonelli headed Mercedes team-mate George Russell in first practice at the penultimate race of the season in Qatar. The 20-year-old Italian posted his fastest time of 1:23.217 on the medium tyre, while Russell's marker, 0.507 seconds adrift, was set on the soft compound. Red Bull's Isack Hadjar finished third, more than six tenths back on Antonelli, with McLaren's Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri fourth and fifth, 0.850 and 0.860 seconds back. Four-time world champion Max Verstappen ended his session three places lower than team-mate Hadjar in sixth, almost a second off the pace, and complained of shaking on the rear axle of his car. Drivers will be limited to a maximum of 27 laps on a set of tyres at the Lusail International Circuit, meaning teams will have to make at least two pit stops during the 57-lap grand prix on Sunday, which starts at 16:00 GMT. Russell says Verstappen's criticism 'quite amusing' Ferrari facing 'very challenging times' - Hamilton The decision is caused by concern over the integrity of the Pirelli tyres on the high-speed, 16-corner track. Laps to the grid, formation laps and any laps completed after the end of the race will not be included. Lewis Hamilton asked his Ferrari pit wall if anyone else experienced tyre degradation "because mine is massive", to which his engineer replied: "Yes, much higher than expected on all compounds." Hamilton smashed into a marker board during the opening hour in Qatar, while Aston Martin's Lance Stroll, the Williams of Carlos Sainz and Alex Albon plus Gasly also had moments off the dusty track. Charles Leclerc was seventh quickest, one place above Scuderia team-mate Hamilton, with Racing Bulls rookie Arvid Lindblad and the Alpine of Pierre Gasly completing the top 10 in ninth and 10th. Red Bull were running different specifications of front wing in first practice as they continue their investigation into what caused Hadjar's failure during last weekend's race in Las Vegas. Russell is looking to salvage something from a difficult season which has seen him slip to fourth in the drivers' championship after his early push for the title. He finished ninth in Las Vegas a week ago but the headlines were dominated by his latest fallout with race winner Max Verstappen. The pair exchanged strong words towards each other but on Thursday, Russell said the spat was not something he was looking to continue. Ferrari are also dealing with the aftermath of another on-track incident between seven-time world champion Hamilton and Monegasque Leclerc. The two made contact in Vegas following their collisions in Italy and Mexico and Hamilton conceded himself, Leclerc and team principal Fred Vasseur were facing "very, very challenging times". Qatar and next week's finale in Abu Dhabi are going ahead as planned despite the ongoing conflict between the United States/Israel and Iran. Full first practice res

item.title: Sunderland squad hit by illness ahead of Spurs clash
item.description: Sunderland squad hit by illness ahead of Spurs clash Sunderland boss Régis Le Bris says several players are struggling with a virus ahead of Sunday’s Premier League clash with Tottenham. The Black Cats are already managing a number of injury concerns during a busy run of fixtures, with Le Bris confirming some members of the squad are now also battling illness. “At the minute we have a few players on the edge with viruses,” he said. “It’s different for everyone, some can play and the others will struggle. At the minute we have a few players like that. I hope they will be fine for this weekend.” Omar Alderete was forced off during Thursday night’s Europa League draw with Jagiellonia after suffering dizziness, but Le Bris confirmed the defender has been assessed and is fine. “He’s been assessed this morning and he’s fine,” he said. Le Bris also provided updates on Romaine Mundle, Dan Ballard, Granit Xhaka and Brian Brobbey. “Romaine and Ballard are running on the pitch, but we won’t rush the process,” he said. “Brian and Granit want to play as soon as possible, but if we can’t sustain the rest of the season it doesn’t make sense.”

item.title: Fabrizio Romano: Liverpool ‘already discussing’ next steps under Andoni Iraola
item.description: Fabrizio Romano: Liverpool ‘already discussing’ next steps under Andoni Iraola Andoni Iraola Earning Liverpool Trust as Long Term Planning Begins Liverpool have moved quickly to stabilise the mood around Anfield, and the early signs under Andoni Iraola are encouraging. According to Fabrizio Romano, the club’s senior figures are pleased with what they have seen from the new head coach, and that matters because this is about more than a decent run of results. It is about direction, authority and whether Liverpool finally look coherent again. Romano’s key line was clear: “They are already discussing with Andoni Iraola about future plans and what they want to do. They are delighted with the coach and the coach is delighted with the Liverpool project. [He has] very good connections with the players.” That tells you two things. First, there is internal alignment. Second, this is not being treated as a short term fix. Liverpool Results Show Real Progress It has been close to six months since Iraola replaced Arne Slot, and the numbers are solid. Liverpool sit fourth in the Premier League, just one point off second, they are well placed to reach the Champions League last 16 automatically, and they are through to the Carabao Cup quarter-finals. Add in penalty shootouts and he has won 12 of his first 18 matches, with only three defeats. Those figures do not prove anything on their own, but they do show competence, and after the chaos of the end of last season, competence is a serious improvement. Liverpool look sharper, more connected and more purposeful. There is structure in and out of possession, and there is less of the drift that damaged the side previously. Andoni Iraola Impact on Key Players The biggest positive may be individual improvement. Alexander Isak looks increasingly decisive, Florian Wirtz is influencing games with more regularity, and Alexis Mac Allister appears refreshed after a difficult end to the previous campaign. When Liverpool’s best players are performing like elite players, the whole team changes shape. This is where coaches earn credibility. Tactical ideas are fine, but players need to look better under your management than they did before. Right now, several Liverpool players do. That is why the praise from inside the club carries weight. Transfer Plans Already Point to Stability Iraola only signed a two-year deal, which raised eyebrows at the time. In reality, that suited his track record and suited a club that had just been burned badly. Shorter contracts can still produce long term thinking if both sides are convinced by the process. The fact discussions are already taking place over transfer plans for 2027 and beyond suggests Liverpool believe they have found a coach worth building with. That does not guarantee anything by spring. Football moves fast, and reputations collapse quickly when results turn. But for now, Liverpool have a head coach improving players, collecting wins and restoring order. That is a very good start.

item.title: The Anaheim Ducks Are Getting One Of The NHL’s Most Exciting Young Forwards Back
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Cutter Gauthier’s historic November has received plenty of attention, but the Anaheim Ducks have another 22-year-old or younger forward producing at better than a point-per-game pace this season. Beckett Sennecke is expected to return to the Ducks’ lineup Friday against the Los Angeles Kings after missing three games with an upper-body injury. Head coach Joel Quenneville confirmed Thursday that Sennecke is ready to return, according to Zach Cavanagh of The Sporting Tribune. The 20-year-old has scored 12 goals and registered 14 assists through 22 games this season after finishing third in Calder Trophy voting with 23 goals and 60 points in 82 games last season. He’s nearly doubled his goal-scoring rate and is on pace for 99 points over a full 84-game schedule. Less than three years ago, Sennecke was playing junior hockey with the Oshawa Generals. He’s now producing at a rate that would’ve put him among the NHL’s leading scorers in most seasons. Sennecke has some ridiculous puck skills, and 10 of his 12 goals this season have come from high-danger areas. According to NHL EDGE, that ties him with Auston Matthews for second in the league, just one behind Artturi Lehkonen. He’s also been on the ice for 22 power-play goals, one fewer than Gauthier. The Ducks lead the NHL with a 33.7% power play, and Sennecke was back practicing with the first unit Thursday. With Leo Carlsson sidelined by an upper-body injury, NHL.com has Sennecke projected to play alongside Gauthier and Roger McQueen on Friday. That’s three forwards selected inside the top 10 of their respective drafts, none of whom are older than 22. McQueen, the 10th overall pick in 2025, scored against the San Jose Sharks on Wednesday and could benefit from playing between two of the league’s most productive young wingers. There aren’t many better linemates for a young center trying to establish himself offensively in the NHL right now. The Ducks lost consecutive 3-2 games against the Utah Mammoth and Seattle Kraken in Sennecke’s absence before beating San Jose 7-0 on Wednesday. They enter Friday’s game with a 12-13-1 record despite the offensive production they’ve been getting from their young forwards. Anaheim has two games against Los Angeles this weekend, and with Carlsson still out, Quenneville could give us our first extended look at what Gauthier, McQueen and Sennecke can do together. item.title: Everton vs Liverpool: Match Preview, Latest Team News and Score Prediction
item.description: Everton vs Liverpool: Match Preview, Latest Team News and Score Prediction Everton vs Liverpool Preview: Isak, Wirtz and Derby Pressure at Hill Dickinson Stadium The Merseyside derby rarely needs dressing up. It has history, edge and a bad habit of dragging everyone into a fight. This latest meeting arrives with Liverpool in better shape, Everton carrying damage from a heavy defeat, and one obvious question hanging over it, can David Moyes patch enough holes to slow a side that has started to find rhythm under Andoni Iraola. There is context here. Everton supporters still had their moment in the final derby at Goodison Park, snatching a late 2-2 draw and making sure the old place signed off with noise. Liverpool, for their part, answered back in the first meeting at Hill Dickinson Stadium last season. So this is not short on recent grievance. The table matters too. Liverpool smashed Manchester United 4-0 at Anfield last Sunday. Everton then lost 4-0 at Brentford. One side comes in with momentum, the other with bruises. With rivals around them in action later, Liverpool know a win gives them a chance to move from fourth to second. Simple enough. Kick-off time and how to watch Everton vs Liverpool Kick-off is at 12pm GMT on Sunday, November 29 at Hill Dickinson Stadium. It is an early start, so anyone expecting the usual 2pm Sunday routine will miss the opening stages. In the UK, the match is live on TNT Sports 1, with coverage beginning at 10.30am. Radio commentary is also available elsewhere. Photo: IMAGO Everton team news with Tarkowski suspended Start with the problem. James Tarkowski is out after his straight red card at Brentford. That matters. Everton lose their most rugged centre-back, a player who relishes exactly this kind of fixture, and they lose him for the first game of a three-match ban. Michael Keane is the obvious replacement, but obvious does not always mean reassuring. There is at least one return. Jack Grealish is available again after coming on at half-time against Brentford following a month out for a breach of club discipline. He is pushing for a start. Everton need more than one player to lift them, though. They were ripped apart a day ago and now face a front line in far better working order. Liverpool team news as Isak and Wirtz lead attack Liverpool had one annoyance in midweek despite beating Club Brugge 3-0. Victor Munoz limped off after treatment on his knee and is now a major doubt. Cody Gakpo is out with the calf injury suffered on international duty, while Ryan Gravenberch remains a doubt. Hugo Ekitike is sidelined with an Achilles problem until January. Conor Bradley and Giovanni Leoni are back in parts of training after long-term injuries, but Iraola has already made it clear both still need work. No mystery there, partial training is not match fitness. The bigger point is that Liverpool still have enough. item.title: Norris Is Not Best in Performing Donuts But Names Supercars-NASCAR Racer Who Is
item.description: Lando Norris said Shane van Gisbergen is the best at donuts and burnouts, and called his own celebrations in Abu Dhabi terrible, at the Qatar Grand Prix media day on Nov. 26. The media reminded McLaren ’s Norris of performing a donut in Abu Dhabi last year against the will of his race engineer. It was not the perfect one, but he won the 2025 F1 title, so it made sense for him to defy his team to celebrate his victory. However, it was not the perfect donut by Norris. He accepted that he was not good at it. But he named the person he thinks is good at it – Shane van Gisbergen . The New Zealander is famous for his wild burnout after post-race victories. Norris Says Someone Else Can Do Better Donuts While doing so, Van Gisbergen climbs out of his race car to salute the crowd. He has multiple Supercars title wins in Australia and has moved to compete in the NASCAR Cup Series. “Mine were terrible [in Abu Dhabi],” said Norris to the media in Qatar. Shane van Gisbergen in the No. 97 car. Image Credit: Daylon Barr / Red Bull Content Pool “Also, because Will (race engineer) asked me not to do a doughnut, so yeah, I was a little bit afraid at that point of doing anything silly, but I did, like two, I think. I’m certainly not the best at doing doughnuts either. “I think the best person at doing celebrations is Shane van Gisbergen, so if you want to know how to do donut, burnouts, blow out the engine, blow out the tires. He’s, yeah, I would say he’s probably my hero in terms of doing celebrations well. “And yeah, he’s certainly the best in many different ways,” Norris said. When asked about performing doughnuts in the 2026 generation of F1 cars, the Brit didn’t know if it would be feasible due to the battery, but advised what can still be done. Current F1 Cars Make Donuts Complicated “So, donut — I wouldn’t even know how to tell you that well, because it’s difficult when you kind of got a hand clutch and all these different things,” said Norris. “And when you got boost and battery, and all, certainly doesn’t make it easier, but just go full, pull the clutch in and yeah, use the full 1,000 horsepower you got behind you.”

item.title: A Tale of Two Kickers on Thanksgiving Night
item.description: William Purnell-Imagn Images Thanksgiving night in Buffalo turned into a tale of two kickers , and only one delivered. While the headlines promised a battle between Josh Allen and Patrick Mahomes, the real story ended with Harrison Butker missing a 46-yard attempt and Tyler Bass hitting a 57-yard winner as time expired. The Bills beat the Chiefs 13-10 in the rain, a result that feels like a slap in the face for Kansas City’s special teams unit. Butker has been a disappointment this season, missing eight field goals in 2026. That total is tied for the most in the league (or leads, depending on whether extra-point misses are included). He hasn’t made a single kick exceeding 50 yards this year, rendering his rainy-night failure predictable instead of shocking. Meanwhile, Bass has been nearly perfect, going 26-for-27 this season. The performance gap was more than one bad night; it was a season-long trend that finally caught up with the Chiefs. Chiefs coach Andy Reid said after the loss that he wasn’t ready to say whether Butker will remain the kicker in Kansas City . “I’ll go back and go through all of it again,” Reid said immediately after the game. He added, “Not gonna make any decisions right this minute.” This hesitation is baffling when you look at the numbers. Since a kicker must successfully make his kicks, Butker is simply failing to perform. The Chiefs had other chances to win, but special teams issues cost them. A controversial call wiped out a huge catch by Rashee Rice, and a fumbled snap by Mahomes derailed a late drive. Yet, the missed field goal by Butker loomed large. Bills Climb While Chiefs Stumble Securing this victory puts Buffalo at 10-1, maintaining their position in the driver’s seat for the AFC’s No. 1 seed. The Chiefs fell to 8-3, now half a game behind the Denver Broncos in the AFC West. Weather played a part, with freezing rain and wind making conditions nasty for everyone. Josh Allen struggled through one of his poorest passing games, while Mahomes managed 174 yards but could not secure the win. James Cook ran for 117 yards and scored the only touchdown for Buffalo, but the game was ultimately decided by the feet. The Bills overcame a sluggish offense to win on the special teams play of the year. Traveling to Los Angeles to play the Rams next Thursday night means the Chiefs will receive no additional rest.

item.title: Meet Ime Udoka, Nigerian-American coach leading Houston Rockets in the NBA
item.description: Nigerian-American basketball coach Ime Udoka has built an impressive career in basketball, rising from representing Nigeria on the international stage to coaching some of the biggest teams in the National Basketball Association (NBA). Udoka, who currently serves as head coach of the Houston Rockets, has established himself as one of the prominent coaching figures in American basketball, with a career shaped by years of playing, coaching and leadership experience. Born on August 9, 1977, in Portland, Oregon, United States, Udoka has Nigerian roots and represented Nigeria in international basketball competitions before transitioning into coaching. His playing career included spells in the NBA, the NBA Development League and professional basketball leagues in Europe. He also played for Nigeria at the 2005 and 2011 FIBA AfroBasket tournaments, helping raise the country’s profile in international basketball. After retiring from professional basketball, Udoka moved into coaching, beginning his NBA coaching career as an assistant with the San Antonio Spurs in 2012. He worked under legendary coach Gregg Popovich, gaining experience in player development, team management and tactical preparation. During his time with San Antonio, the Spurs reached the NBA Finals in 2013 and won the championship in 2014, providing Udoka with valuable experience at the highest level of the sport. He subsequently served as an assistant coach with the Philadelphia 76ers and Brooklyn Nets before joining the Boston Celtics in 2021. Led Boston Celtics to NBA Finals Udoka’s breakthrough as a head coach came in 2021 when he was appointed to lead the Boston Celtics. In his first season, he guided the team to the 2022 NBA Finals, where they faced the Golden State Warriors. Although Boston lost the series 4-2, Udoka earned recognition for transforming the team’s defensive performance and guiding its players through a successful playoff campaign. His achievement made him one of the few coaches to reach the NBA Finals in his first season as a head coach. However, his tenure in Boston ended in September 2022 when the franchise suspended him for the 2022–23 season over violations of team policies. New chapter with Houston Rockets In April 2023, the Houston Rockets appointed Udoka as their head coach, giving him another opportunity to lead an NBA franchise. He took charge of a rebuilding team that had struggled in previous seasons and was tasked with improving its competitiveness through tactical discipline, player development and stronger defensive organisation. His appointment marked another significant milestone in his coaching career, as he became responsible for developing a young Houston squad and guiding the franchise towards sustained success. Udoka’s coaching approach has been associated with defensive intensity, accountability and high expectations for players. item.description: Affordable laptops are even more affordable right now. | Photo: Antonio G. Di Benedetto / The Verge Laptop prices have been a hot-button topic all year long thanks to RAMageddon . We’ve seen existing models get more expensive and new models arrive at higher prices than last-gen — sometimes with lower specs, too. 2026 in general has been a bad time to buy a computer. But thankfully, Black Friday can offer a tiny bit of respite. If the computer you currently use is working well for you, good. Happy for you. But if you’re in the market for something more powerful, bigger, smaller, thinner, etc. — and you prefer new over used — you can currently save some decent dough on MacBooks, Windows notebooks, and gaming laptops. The big, multi-hundred-dollar savings are typically reserved for higher-end models with bigger specs, like Windows models running Nvidia’s new Arm-based RTX Spark platform — which are getting their first major discounts. More budget-friendly laptops are also receiving decent discounts right now, though, including the MacBook Neo. The current $100 discount on Apple’s budget laptop might seem like small potatoes considering it’s just a return to its original price , but it’s the best you can do for now (if you can’t hold out for a rumored new one in 2027 ). As always, the deals below are for laptops we’ve reviewed or tested firsthand in some way at The Verge — either that exact model or a similar one we expect to be equally good. There are many laptops out there and myriad deals running now through Cyber Monday, but if any of these fit your needs, you can’t go wrong. item.title: NASA’s NG-25 Mission to Launch Pioneering Space Crops Research
item.description: Experiments in the Ohalo III facility (pictured above) aim to validate plant-water delivery, optimize volume, and advance crop-production research. These insights could inform the design of plant production systems for future deep-space missions. NASA NASA experiments, including a first-of-its-kind space crop production system, will travel to the International Space Station aboard Northrop Grumman’s 25th Commercial Resupply Services mission for the agency. Investigations from NASA’s Biological and Physical Sciences Division will advance research that benefits life on Earth and future exploration, expanding knowledge of space crops and human health. Groundbreaking space crops Astronauts will need sustainable sources of food to travel farther and stay longer in space. To help understand how crop production works in microgravity, NASA is launching a novel space crops experiment . The new prototype growth chamber will provide critical insights for developing safe, nutritious, and reliable crop production systems for future Moon Base habitats and Mars missions. Knowledge gained from the space crop production system also could help inform agricultural practices such as vertical farming and indoor growing systems. Researchers will use this investigation to validate the system’s water delivery and volume optimization technology aboard the space station. Tiny brain models aboard station A precision health investigation is the next step toward enabling long-duration studies of human brain tissues in space. The research builds on a previous investigation that sent small, lab-grown models of the human brain, called miBrains, to the space station. This experiment will validate a miniature fluid-handling system designed to mix, deliver, and maintain the nutrient-rich liquid needed to keep the tissues alive. Researchers could use the findings to help identify potential neurological risks associated with spaceflight and develop strategies to protect astronaut health. It also may advance human tissue research and neurological disease modeling on Earth. Biological & Physical Sciences Division NASA’s Biological and Physical Sciences Division pioneers scientific discovery and enables exploration by using space environments to conduct investigations not possible on Earth. Studying biological and physical phenomena under extreme conditions allows researchers to advance the fundamental scientific knowledge required to go farther and stay longer in space, while also benefitting life on Earth.

item.title: Nigeria’s future depends on mentally resilient youths — Mamora
item.description: Former minister urges graduates to embrace purpose, adaptability, continuous learning By Adeola Badru Former Minister of Health, Olorunnimbe Mamora, has said Nigeria’s future depends largely on the mental resilience, character development and sense of purpose of its youths, warning that academic qualifications alone are insufficient to prepare them for the challenges of the modern world. Mamora said young Nigerians must develop the capacity to navigate economic uncertainties, technological disruptions and changing employment opportunities through adaptability, continuous learning and problem-solving skills. He spoke while delivering the 18th Convocation Lecture of Ajayi Crowther University (ACU), Oyo, titled, “Youths’ Mental Health and Purpose: Thriving in a Volatile World.” The former minister challenged graduating students to look beyond the certificates they had earned and prepare for a world where success would increasingly depend on their ability to manage uncertainty, identify opportunities and remain relevant. He described convocation as a transition into a new phase of life, requiring graduates to demonstrate resilience, discipline, adaptability and a clear sense of purpose. Mamora identified the growing influence of social media, economic pressures and rapid technological advancement as emerging challenges to the mental wellbeing of young people. While acknowledging that the internet had expanded access to information and opportunities, he noted that excessive engagement with digital platforms could contribute to loneliness, anxiety and unhealthy comparisons. He urged graduates not to measure their achievements or personal worth against the lifestyles and apparent successes of others on social media. “Do not allow social media platforms to become the mirror through which you measure your worth. “Your value is not determined by the number of people who like your photograph. Stop comparing your backstage with somebody else’s stage,” he said. On the changing employment landscape, particularly with the emergence of Artificial Intelligence (AI), Mamora said graduates must recognise that education should go beyond acquiring academic qualifications. He stressed the importance of critical thinking, problem-solving, skills acquisition and continuous learning, noting that adaptability would be essential to remaining relevant in the evolving world of work. Drawing inspiration from the life of Bishop Samuel Ajayi Crowther, after whom the university was named, Mamora said the cleric’s journey from slavery to becoming a renowned missionary and scholar demonstrated the importance of determination and resilience in overcoming adversity. He urged the graduates to draw inspiration from Crowther’s life and remain committed to their aspirations despite the challenges they might encounter. item.title: Omo-Agege denies snubbing police invitation over Uduere killings
item.description: Senator Ovie Omo-Agege has denied reports claiming he refused to honour an invitation from the Delta State Police Command over Monday’s attack on members of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, at Uduere. In a statement on Friday by his Media Adviser, Sunny Areh, the former Deputy President of the Senate said he had seen the reports and described them as untrue. “Senator Ovie Omo-Agege has seen the reports claiming he refused to honour an invitation from the Delta State Police Command over Monday’s attack on members of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, at Uduere. “It isn’t true. You can’t turn down an invitation you never received,” he said. According to the statement, no formal invitation has reached the Senator or his office. “No letter has reached the Senator or his office, and no officer has come to him with one. He first learned of it the same way everyone else did, from the Command’s announcement in the media.” Areh said the report that Omo-Agege refused to appear was based on a single unnamed source. “The claim that he refused leans on a single unnamed source. The Senator hasn’t told the police, or anyone else, that he won’t appear.” The statement also revisited the events at Uduere, insisting that Omo-Agege was the victim of the attack. “It is worth remembering what happened at Uduere. Senator Omo-Agege was the target of an assassination attempt. Senior members of his campaign team were murdered, and others are still in hospital with serious injuries. “He is the one who survived an attack on his life, and the one demanding that those responsible be found and prosecuted.” Omo-Agege said he wants the case resolved and justice for the victims. “He wants this case resolved, and he wants justice for the dead and the wounded. If the police serve a lawful invitation, he will honour it. He asks only that it be sent through his office so a date can be agreed.” He faulted the manner in which the alleged invitation was made public. “A summons announced in the press before it reaches the person named is not due process, and he won’t be tried in the media,” he said. item.title: 2027: National Counter Terrorism Centre moves to foil attacks on INEC facilities, personnel
item.description: ..Laka warns against electoral violence, voter intimidation, destruction of infrastructure By Kingsley Omonobi The National Counter Terrorism Centre (NCTC), Office of the National Security Adviser, has said it is working with security agencies to prevent planned attacks on Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) offices, personnel and electoral infrastructure ahead of the 2027 general elections. The National Coordinator of the Centre, Major General Adamu Laka, also said measures were being strengthened to protect voters and prevent emerging security threats from disrupting the electoral process. Laka spoke at the National Flag-off/North Central Zone Town Hall Engagement on Preventing Electoral Violence and Strengthening Election Security in Nigeria. He urged youths not to allow themselves to be used as instruments of political violence, describing them as critical stakeholders in the country’s democratic future. “In this regard, I urge our young people not to allow themselves to be used as instruments of political violence. You are important stakeholders in Nigeria’s democratic future and your energy, creativity and influence should be directed towards promoting peace, tolerance and responsible civic participation,” he said. He said the Centre was working towards preventing attacks on INEC offices and personnel, protecting voters and electoral infrastructure, countering fake news and inflammatory narratives, strengthening community-based early warning systems and ensuring timely responses to emerging security threats. Describing elections as the heartbeat of democracy, Laka said their credibility depended not only on the conduct of voting and announcement of results but also on the peace, security and public confidence surrounding the entire electoral process. “There is absolutely no gain in any loss of life or property as a result of this democratic process,” he said. The NCTC coordinator identified misinformation and disinformation, hate speech, political intolerance, incitement, youth manipulation, political thuggery, vote buying, voter intimidation, voter suppression and destruction of public infrastructure as factors that could fuel electoral violence. He said stakeholders must collectively address the threats and strengthen early warning and response mechanisms to identify potential dangers before they escalate into violence. Laka also stressed the need to build public confidence in the electoral process and ensure that women, youths, persons with disabilities and internally displaced persons were not excluded from meaningful participation. He maintained that preventing electoral violence was not the responsibility of security agencies alone but required the collective commitment of political actors, government institutions, traditional and religious leaders, civil society organisations, the media and community-based organisations.
